Pi's session files are JSONL and live under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, not directly in `~/.pi`. The search didn't turn up a dedicated hooks directory, so I can't confirm where hooks live.

- **Session location:** The official format doc gives the path pattern as a per-project folder under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, with each file named by timestamp and UUID (~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path>--/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl, where the path is the working directory with slashes replaced by dashes).
- **File structure:** Each line is a JSON object tagged with a `type` field, and entries link through `id` and `parentId` (each line is a JSON object with a type field; session entries form a tree via id/parentId fields). That tree is what allows branching without new files.
- **Deleting sessions:** You can remove the `.jsonl` files directly, or use `/resume` and press Ctrl+D. Pi uses the `trash` CLI when it's available (to avoid permanent deletion).
- **Extensions:** Extensions are TypeScript and can be bundled into shareable Pi Packages. Pi's docs say that Pi Packages can hold extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes and be shared via npm or git. Version 3 of the session format also renamed the `hookMessage` role to `custom` as part of extensions unification.
- **Hooks:** One comparison table lists pi's extensibility as "TypeScript extensions + packages" against other tools' "Hooks + MCP," which suggests pi handles this through extensions rather than a separate hooks system. That source is a third-party docs site, so treat it as unconfirmed.

The package is `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`, installed with npm. Most of the results are mirrored npm READMEs and third-party write-ups rather than the official pi.dev site, so check the upstream repo (badlogic/pi-mono) before relying on the details.

Tôi đã nhận yêu cầu thêm Antigravity, pi và omp, và đang khảo sát cả ba trước khi lập plan bổ sung. Researcher còn đang chạy, chưa có kết quả.

**Những gì đã biết:**
- Cả ba đều đã cài trên máy này (`pi`, `omp`, `agy`).
- pi và omp lưu phiên dạng JSONL, thư mục con đặt tên theo thư mục làm việc: pi ở `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, omp ở `~/.omp/agent/sessions/`. Cả hai không có hook dạng lệnh shell như Claude Code; muốn tự gom sau phiên phải viết một extension TypeScript. [Pi session format](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.64.0/docs/session.md), [omp trên cmux](https://cmux.com/docs/agent-integrations/oh-my-pi).
- Antigravity khó nhất. Tài liệu chính thức có mục Hooks nhưng tôi chưa đọc được nội dung, và cách lưu hội thoại ở bản CLI khác bản IDE: có nguồn nói JSONL, có nguồn nói `.pb` (protobuf). Nếu bản IDE chỉ có `.pb` thì có thể phải giải mã ngược định dạng mới đọc được. [Antigravity CLI docs](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/cli/commands/resume), [DEV tutorial](https://dev.to/iromin/antigravity-cli-tutorial-series-part-2-conversations-conversations-and-conversations-j39).

Tôi không sửa được câu goal vì nó do bạn đặt; tôi coi ba công cụ này là phần việc thêm vào mục tiêu đang chạy.

**Kết quả mới từ trước khi nhận yêu cầu này:**
- Codex chưa từng chạy hook của momentry, trên mọi nền tảng: `hooks.json` của Codex đòi tên sự kiện dạng `PreCompact`, `SessionEnd`, `SessionStart`, còn momentry ghi `pre_compact`, `session_start` nên bị bỏ qua mà không báo gì. Đã sửa (thêm cả `SessionEnd`) và đã push; CI vẫn xanh.
- Dù vậy, khi chạy thử trên Windows (với `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`), phiên `codex exec` không đăng nhập vẫn không gọi hook. Nhiều khả năng nó dừng trước bước hook, nhưng chưa chứng minh được. Phần Codex vẫn để trong [issue #1](https://github.com/vantt/momentry/issues/1).
- `README.md` và `README.vi.md` còn ghi `pre_compact` cho Codex. Tôi không sửa vì hai file này đang có thay đổi dở của phiên làm README song ngữ; phiên đó nên sửa luôn chỗ này.

Khi researcher xong, tôi lập plan cho ba công cụ dựa trên kết quả, rồi làm như đã làm với Claude Code và Codex: viết bộ đọc transcript, cài hook hoặc extension, thêm `/bip`, test, CI.

- **Transcripts:** JSONL at `<agentDir>/sessions/--<encoded cwd>--/<ts>_<uuid>.jsonl`. `agentDir` is `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` or `~/.pi/agent`; `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` or the `sessionDir` setting makes the folder flat.

**omp** (v18.12.6)
- **Transcripts:** same format as pi, but the first line is a padded `title` line, and the folder name encodes cwd differently. Named profiles live under `~/.omp/profiles/<p>/agent`.
- **Reader rules:** drop user messages with `attribution:"agent"` (576 of 636 locally are injected, not typed). Drop the 6,315 `tool_execution_start` noise entries. Take edit paths from the tool result's `details.path`.

137	
138	- **pi**:
139	  - `--no-extensions` or a missing per-account directory silently disables the integration.
140	  - A custom `sessionDir` produces a flat directory, so the backfill scan needs those roots too; hooks pass the path, so they are unaffected.

142	- **omp**:
143	  - Named profiles ignore `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
144	  - A file rewrite (migration, discard, contested lease, or move) can shift line numbers without shrinking the file. The ledger only resets on shrink, so a window could misalign. This is rare; mitigate later by storing the header id plus the line count.
145	  - Interactive extensions may bind after the composer opens. `session_start` is still delivered.
146	  - `.jsonl.gz` archives are skipped.
147	- **agy**:
148	  - Hooks are synchronous. Keep the hook under the 10-second timeout; it already returns in about 100 ms.
149	  - On Windows, hooks run via `cmd /c`, with cwd set to the `hooks.json` directory, never the repo. Always use `workspacePaths`.
150	  - The workspace `.agents/hooks.json` needs folder trust; global hooks do not.
151	  - The transcript format is undocumented beyond the embedded agent docs and may change.

- The IDE is covered by the same global `hooks.json`. Its payload `transcriptPath` points into `antigravity-ide/`, so the reader needs no IDE-specific code. The IDE is not installed locally, so this is unverified.

## Fragility and Windows

- **pi**:
  - `--no-extensions` or a missing per-account directory silently disables the integration.
  - A custom `sessionDir` produces a flat directory, so the backfill scan needs those roots too; hooks pass the path, so they are unaffected.
  - On Windows, the bash tool is Git Bash, so `/bip`'s `momentry` (a `.cmd` shim) may not resolve by bare name. Needs a test.
- **omp**:
  - Named profiles ignore `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
  - A file rewrite (migration, discard, contested lease, or move) can shift line numbers without shrinking the file. The ledger only resets on shrink, so a window could misalign. This is rare; mitigate later by storing the header id plus the line count.
  - Interactive extensions may bind after the composer opens. `session_start` is still delivered.
  - `.jsonl.gz` archives are skipped.
- **agy**:
  - Hooks are synchronous. Keep the hook under the 10-second timeout; it already returns in about 100 ms.
  - On Windows, hooks run via `cmd /c`, with cwd set to the `hooks.json` directory, never the repo. Always use `workspacePaths`.
  - The workspace `.agents/hooks.json` needs folder trust; global hooks do not.
  - The transcript format is undocumented beyond the embedded agent docs and may change.

# Thêm host pi, omp, Antigravity; tự tìm mọi profile

## Overview

User thêm vào goal (2026-11-03): hỗ trợ `antigravity / pi / omp`. Thiết kế theo [báo cáo researcher](../reports/researcher-261103-1750-pi-omp-antigravity-hosts.md).

## Quyết định của user (2026-11-03)

- **agy gom khi mở phiên sau:** hook `SessionStart` ghi phiên vào chỉ mục và quét các phiên agy cũ của repo. Không dùng `Stop` (chạy mỗi lượt, chặn agent).
- **Tự tìm mọi profile:** cài và quét ở thư mục mặc định cùng mọi profile tìm thấy: `~/.codex-*`, `~/.pi/accounts/*`, `~/.omp/profiles/*/agent`, `~/.agy-homes/*/.gemini`; `doctor` báo profile chưa cài.

## Ràng buộc

- Không thêm phụ thuộc; không đọc SQLite/protobuf của agy (chỉ `transcript*.jsonl`).
- Session id của host mới lấy 8 hex cuối của uuid (uuidv7 trùng 8 hex đầu trong ~65 giây). Claude, Codex giữ nguyên để không gãy sổ.
- README.md / README.vi.md đang có thay đổi của phiên khác: không sửa trong plan này.

## Phases

| # | Phase | Status |
|---|-------|--------|
| 1 | [Bộ đọc transcript pi/omp/agy](./phase-01-transcript-readers.md) | Pending |
| 2 | [Hook runtime và tìm profile](./phase-02-hooks-and-profiles.md) | Pending |
| 3 | [Cài extension, hooks.json, /bip](./phase-03-host-integration.md) | Pending |
| 4 | [Test, tài liệu, CI](./phase-04-tests-docs-ci.md) | Pending |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `momentry scan --pi|--omp|--agy` tìm và đọc được phiên của repo (fixture theo đúng schema; thử trên dữ liệu thật trong máy, chỉ đếm, không in nội dung).
- [ ] `momentry init --yes` cài extension `momentry.ts` cho pi/omp, hook `SessionStart` cho agy, `/bip` cho cả ba, vào mọi profile tìm thấy; chạy lại không đổi gì; `uninstall` gỡ sạch.
- [ ] Extension pi/omp gọi `momentry hook … --pi|--omp` với payload chuẩn; hook agy in `{}` và ghi chỉ mục.
- [ ] Test, lifecycle installer, CI 9/9 xanh.

# Thêm host pi, omp, Antigravity; tự tìm mọi profile

## Overview

User thêm vào goal (2026-11-03): hỗ trợ `antigravity / pi / omp`. Thiết kế theo [báo cáo researcher](../reports/researcher-261103-1750-pi-omp-antigravity-hosts.md).

## Quyết định của user (2026-11-03)

- **agy gom khi mở phiên sau:** hook `SessionStart` ghi phiên vào chỉ mục và quét các phiên agy cũ của repo. Không dùng `Stop` (chạy mỗi lượt, chặn agent).
- **Tự tìm mọi profile:** cài và quét ở thư mục mặc định cùng mọi profile tìm thấy: `~/.codex-*`, `~/.pi/accounts/*`, `~/.omp/profiles/*/agent`, `~/.agy-homes/*/.gemini`; `doctor` báo profile chưa cài.

## Ràng buộc

- Không thêm phụ thuộc; không đọc SQLite/protobuf của agy (chỉ `transcript*.jsonl`).
- Session id của host mới lấy 8 hex cuối của uuid (uuidv7 trùng 8 hex đầu trong ~65 giây). Claude, Codex giữ nguyên để không gãy sổ.
- README.md / README.vi.md đang có thay đổi của phiên khác: không sửa trong plan này.

## Phases

| # | Phase | Status |
|---|-------|--------|
| 1 | [Bộ đọc transcript pi/omp/agy](./phase-01-transcript-readers.md) | Pending |
| 2 | [Hook runtime và tìm profile](./phase-02-hooks-and-profiles.md) | Pending |
| 3 | [Cài extension, hooks.json, /bip](./phase-03-host-integration.md) | Pending |
| 4 | [Test, tài liệu, CI](./phase-04-tests-docs-ci.md) | Pending |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `momentry scan --pi|--omp|--agy` tìm và đọc được phiên của repo (fixture theo đúng schema; thử trên dữ liệu thật trong máy, chỉ đếm, không in nội dung).
- [ ] `momentry init --yes` cài extension `momentry.ts` cho pi/omp, hook `SessionStart` cho agy, `/bip` cho cả ba, vào mọi profile tìm thấy; chạy lại không đổi gì; `uninstall` gỡ sạch.
- [ ] Extension pi/omp gọi `momentry hook … --pi|--omp` với payload chuẩn; hook agy in `{}` và ghi chỉ mục.
- [ ] Test, lifecycle installer, CI 9/9 xanh.

# Phase 1: Bộ đọc transcript pi/omp/agy

## Goal
`lib/sources/pi.mjs` (dùng chung cho pi và omp) và `lib/sources/agy.mjs` theo cùng hợp đồng với `claude.mjs`/`codex.mjs`: `sessionId`, `listTranscripts(repoRoot, opts)`, `readEntries(file, range)`, `countLines`.

- Create: fixture `test/fixtures/transcripts/pi-session.jsonl`, `omp-session.jsonl`, `agy/transcript_full.jsonl` (bịa, đúng schema).

- [ ] pi/omp reader + test
- [ ] agy reader + chỉ mục + test
- [ ] pipeline/scan/sourceOf + test
- [ ] Thử trên dữ liệu thật trong máy: đếm Entry theo loại, không in nội dung

## Files
- Modify: `lib/hook.mjs` — runtime mới; agy: chuẩn hoá `conversationId`/`transcriptPath`/`workspacePaths[0]`, ghi chỉ mục, in `{}`, tách nền `scan --agy --except`.
- Modify: `bin`/`lib/cli.mjs` runHook (cờ mới; agy cần stdout `{}`).
- Create: `lib/profiles.mjs` — `hostRoots(name, env)`: claude `[CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR||~/.claude]`; codex `[CODEX_HOME||~/.codex, ~/.codex-*]`; pi `[PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR||~/.pi/agent, ~/.pi/accounts/*]`; omp `[~/.omp/agent, ~/.omp/profiles/*/agent]`; agy `[~/.gemini, ~/.agy-homes/*/.gemini]`; chỉ giữ thư mục tồn tại.

- [ ] hook runtime pi/omp/agy + test
- [ ] scan đọc transcript ở mọi profile

- `node --test test/hook.test.mjs test/paths.test.mjs`

# Phase 3: Cài extension, hooks.json, /bip

## Goal
`hosts.mjs` cài/gỡ theo từng thư mục profile: Claude/Codex như cũ (nay cho mọi profile); pi/omp ghi `<agentDir>/extensions/momentry.ts` (file sở hữu theo dòng đánh dấu sha256 như `bip.md`); agy ghi mục `momentry` vào `<home>/.gemini/config/hooks.json`; `/bip` ở `<agentDir>/prompts/bip.md` (pi), `<agentDir>/commands/bip.md` (omp), `<home>/.gemini/config/skills/bip/SKILL.md` (agy, `disable-model-invocation: true`).

## Files
- Modify: `lib/hosts.mjs`, `lib/checks.mjs` (một check mỗi host, liệt kê profile chưa cài), `lib/uninstall.mjs`, `lib/commands.mjs` (`connect [claude|codex|pi|omp|agy]`).
- Create: `prompts/pi-extension.ts` (mẫu), `prompts/agy-bip.md`.

## Tasks & Steps
- [ ] hosts.mjs đa profile, đa kiểu cài
- [ ] extension pi/omp: gọi node tuyệt đối + `bin/momentry.mjs` (omp chạy Bun; Windows không spawn `.cmd`)

- [ ] doctor/uninstall
- [ ] Thử thật: `omp`/`pi` nạp extension không lỗi (chế độ không gọi model nếu có), agy hooks.json hợp lệ

## Verification
- `node --test test/hosts.test.mjs`; `sh scripts/test-installer.sh`
EOF

+- Host mới: **pi**, **omp (oh-my-pi)**, **Antigravity**. `momentry scan --pi|--omp|--agy` đọc transcript của chúng; `init`/`connect` cài extension `momentry.ts` cho pi/omp, hook `SessionStart` cho Antigravity và `/bip` cho cả ba.
+- Cài và quét ở **mọi profile**: `~/.codex-*`, `~/.pi/accounts/*`, `~/.omp/profiles/*/agent`, `~/.agy-homes/*/.gemini`; `doctor` báo profile chưa cài.
- `momentry quarantine --release all`: kiểm lại mọi chuyện đang bị giữ, thả chuyện sạch vào hộp, chuyện còn vi phạm vẫn bị giữ (thoát 1 nếu còn chuyện bị giữ).

**`/bip`:** một lệnh slash cho Claude (`~/.claude/commands/bip.md`) và prompt tương ứng cho Codex (`~/.codex/prompts/bip.md`), do `init`/`connect` cài. Lệnh này bảo agent gọi `momentry add --by human --note "<ghi chú>"`, tạo ngay một chuyện `captured_by: human`, `hit_by: [bip]`. `add` cũng qua bộ kiểm riêng tư (mục 6.7). Trên Claude, dòng `/bip` trong transcript còn thành điểm nóng loại `bip` ở lần gom sau (mục 5.3). Trên Codex chỉ có đường `add`.

+**Host thêm (quyết định của user 2026-11-03):** pi, omp (oh-my-pi), Antigravity. pi/omp không có hook lệnh shell: momentry ghi extension `extensions/momentry.ts` gọi `momentry hook <event> --pi|--omp` khi `session_start`, `session_before_compact`, `session_shutdown`. Antigravity chỉ có `SessionStart` và `Stop` (chạy mỗi lượt, chặn agent): chỉ dùng `SessionStart`, ghi chỉ mục phiên (transcript không có cwd) và gom các phiên agy trước đó của repo. momentry cài và quét ở mọi profile tìm thấy (`~/.codex-*`, `~/.pi/accounts/*`, `~/.omp/profiles/*/agent`, `~/.agy-homes/*/.gemini`). Session id của host mới lấy 8 hex cuối của uuid (UUIDv7 trùng 8 hex đầu trong khoảng 65 giây). Chi tiết: [installation.md](installation.md#host-được-hỗ-trợ).

**Repo được quan sát** **(mặc định, user có thể đổi):** chỉ repo có file `.momentry.json` ở git root (có thể là `{}`), hoặc nằm trong biến `MOMENTRY_REPOS` (danh sách đường dẫn, phân cách `:`; `;` trên Windows). Lý do: hook cài ở mức user sẽ chạy trong mọi repo, không nên tự ghi thư mục mới vào repo không liên quan. `momentry init` tạo file này.

content.text:
Cả hai việc bạn thêm vào goal đã xong, đã push, và CI xanh 9/9 (Linux, macOS, Windows × Node 20/22/24).

**1. `momentry quarantine --release all`:** kiểm lại riêng tư cho mọi chuyện đang bị giữ ngoài repo. Chuyện sạch được đưa vào hộp; chuyện còn vi phạm vẫn bị giữ, kèm lý do đã che tên. Lệnh thoát 1 nếu vẫn còn chuyện bị giữ, và có `--json`.

**2. Thêm pi, omp và Antigravity, cài vào mọi profile:**
- `momentry scan` đọc được transcript của cả ba host mới. Tôi đã thử trên dữ liệu thật trong máy, chỉ đếm số dòng và loại, không đọc nội dung.
- `momentry init` / `momentry connect` cài cho từng host:
  - **pi và omp:** extension `extensions/momentry.ts`, vì hai host này không có hook lệnh shell. Extension báo cho momentry lúc mở phiên, trước compact và lúc kết thúc phiên.
  - **Antigravity:** hook `SessionStart` trong nhóm `"momentry"` của `config/hooks.json`. Theo lựa chọn của bạn, một phiên agy được gom khi bạn mở phiên agy kế tiếp trong repo đó.
  - **`/bip`** cho cả ba host.
- Cài và quét ở mọi profile tìm thấy. Trên máy bạn là 4 thư mục Codex, 9 pi, 10 omp và 4 agy. `doctor` báo profile mới chưa được cài.

**Đã thử với chương trình thật trên Linux:**
- **pi 1.4.0:** nạp extension, và lúc mở phiên thì gọi momentry quét các phiên cũ.
- **omp 18.12.6:** cũng nạp extension và chạy trọn chuỗi: lúc mở phiên thì quét, lúc kết thúc thì gom. momentry đọc được transcript, rồi dừng ở bước gọi model vì môi trường thử không có tài khoản, đúng dự kiến.

**Tìm thêm một lỗi có từ trước:** hook của Codex chưa từng chạy trên bất kỳ máy nào. Codex đòi tên sự kiện dạng `PreCompact`/`SessionStart`, còn momentry ghi `pre_compact`/`session_start`, và Codex bỏ qua mà không báo gì. Đã sửa, đồng thời thêm sự kiện `SessionEnd` (nay Codex đã có). Chạy `momentry connect codex --yes` để cập nhật hook trên máy.

**Chưa kiểm được, đã ghi vào [issue #1](https://github.com/vantt/momentry/issues/1) kèm các bước kiểm:**
- **Antigravity:** `agy` đòi đăng nhập trước khi mở phiên, nên hook chưa chạy được trong môi trường thử. Chỉ đối chiếu được định dạng `hooks.json` với tài liệu chính thức và với nhóm hook `herdr` có sẵn trên máy.
- **Codex:** chưa có phiên Codex thật nào gọi hook.

**Một sai sót của tôi:** khi thử omp, tôi nói sẽ không gửi gì ra ngoài, nhưng omp bỏ qua địa chỉ cục bộ tôi đặt và đã gửi một yêu cầu tới OpenAI với khoá giả (bị từ chối 401). Không có khoá thật nào bị gửi. Lần thử agy sau đó tôi đã cố cô lập mạng, nhưng máy không có công cụ cô lập.

**Bạn cần quyết:** các thay đổi này đang nằm ở mục "Unreleased" của CHANGELOG, chưa có trong bản v0.1.0 đã phát hành. Bạn muốn cắt v0.2.0 ngay (thay đổi tên sự kiện Codex nên tới người dùng sớm), hay chờ kiểm xong issue #1? Ngoài ra, `README.md` và `README.vi.md` vẫn ghi `pre_compact` cho Codex và chưa nhắc tới pi, omp, Antigravity. Tôi không sửa vì hai file đang có thay đổi dở của phiên làm README song ngữ.

- **pi 1.4.0:** nạp extension, và lúc mở phiên thì gọi momentry quét các phiên cũ.
- **omp 18.12.6:** cũng nạp extension và chạy trọn chuỗi: lúc mở phiên thì quét, lúc kết thúc thì gom. momentry đọc được transcript, rồi dừng ở bước gọi model vì môi trường thử không có tài khoản, đúng dự kiến.

**Tìm thêm một lỗi có từ trước:** hook của Codex chưa từng chạy trên bất kỳ máy nào. Codex đòi tên sự kiện dạng `PreCompact`/`SessionStart`, còn momentry ghi `pre_compact`/`session_start`, và Codex bỏ qua mà không báo gì. Đã sửa, đồng thời thêm sự kiện `SessionEnd` (nay Codex đã có). Chạy `momentry connect codex --yes` để cập nhật hook trên máy.

**Chưa kiểm được, đã ghi vào [issue #1](https://github.com/vantt/momentry/issues/1) kèm các bước kiểm:**
- **Antigravity:** `agy` đòi đăng nhập trước khi mở phiên, nên hook chưa chạy được trong môi trường thử. Chỉ đối chiếu được định dạng `hooks.json` với tài liệu chính thức và với nhóm hook `herdr` có sẵn trên máy.
- **Codex:** chưa có phiên Codex thật nào gọi hook.

**Một sai sót của tôi:** khi thử omp, tôi nói sẽ không gửi gì ra ngoài, nhưng omp bỏ qua địa chỉ cục bộ tôi đặt và đã gửi một yêu cầu tới OpenAI với khoá giả (bị từ chối 401). Không có khoá thật nào bị gửi. Lần thử agy sau đó tôi đã cố cô lập mạng, nhưng máy không có công cụ cô lập.

**Bạn cần quyết:** các thay đổi này đang nằm ở mục "Unreleased" của CHANGELOG, chưa có trong bản v0.1.0 đã phát hành. Bạn muốn cắt v0.2.0 ngay (thay đổi tên sự kiện Codex nên tới người dùng sớm), hay chờ kiểm xong issue #1? SP=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-vantt-projects-momentry/ab9a1dd8-2e8c-4156-8f2c-4736da941413/scratchpad/probe-codex
CODEXBIN=$(bash -c 'type -P codex')
for variant in with-config no-config; do
  B=$SP/$variant; mkdir -p $B/home/.codex $B/repo $B/cache
  (cd $B/repo && git init -q && echo '{}' > .momentry.json)
  if [ $variant = with-config ]; then cat > $B/home/.codex/config.toml <<'TOML'
model_provider = "local"
model = "gpt-5"
[model_providers.local]
name = "local"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
TOML
  fi
  run() { env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=$B/home CODEX_HOME=$B/home/.codex MOMENTRY_CACHE=$B/cache MOMENTRY_CONFIG=$B/none.json "$@"; }
  run node /home/vantt/projects/momentry/bin/momentry.mjs connect codex --yes >/dev/null
  cd $B/repo
  echo "=== $variant"

  sleep 3
  echo "--- hook.log"; cut -c1-200 $B/cache/hook.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no hook.log)"
done

p='.github/workflows/windows-hook-probe.yml'; s=open(p).read()

        shell: powershell
        working-directory: probe-repo
        continue-on-error: true

          $roll = Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter 'rollout-*.jsonl' (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex\\sessions') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
          if ($roll) { Select-String -LiteralPath $roll.FullName -Pattern 'hook' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(600, $_.Line.Length)) } }
          $cmdline = (Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex\\hooks.json') | ConvertFrom-Json).hooks.SessionStart[0].hooks[0].command
          Write-Host "command: $cmdline"
          '{"session_id":"x","cwd":"' + ((Get-Location).Path -replace '\\\\','\\\\') + '"}' | cmd.exe /C "`"$cmdline`""
          Write-Host "cmd /C exit: $LASTEXITCODE"
      - name: report hook.log"""
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

        shell: powershell
        working-directory: probe-repo
        run: |
          $codexHome = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex'

          Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $codexHome 'config.toml') -Encoding ASCII -Value @(
            'model_provider = "local"', 'model = "gpt-5"', '[model_providers.local]', 'name = "local"', 'base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"', 'wire_api = "responses"')
          $p = Start-Process -FilePath 'cmd.exe' -ArgumentList '/c','codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust "hello" > codex.out 2>&1' -PassThru -NoNewWindow
          if (-not $p.WaitForExit(90000)) { $p.Kill() }
          Get-Content codex.out -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String 'hook:|failed to parse'

content.text:
Đã phát hành v0.2.0, và cả năm host đã được kiểm bằng chương trình thật. Issue #1 đã đóng.

**Hook chạy thật trên từng host:**

| Host | Nơi kiểm | Kết quả |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Windows | gọi hook lúc mở và kết thúc phiên, gom được transcript |
| Codex v0.166 | Linux, Windows | gọi hook lúc mở và kết thúc phiên |
| pi 1.4.0, omp 18.12.6 | Linux | nạp extension `momentry.ts`, gọi hook |
| Antigravity 1.4.4 | Linux, tài khoản `tetnu` của bạn | gọi hook `SessionStart`, ghi đúng phiên và thư mục repo |

**Kiểm thật lộ ra ba lỗi mới, đã sửa:**
- **Codex trên Windows:** Codex chạy lệnh hook bằng shell của phiên, mặc định là PowerShell. PowerShell hiểu lệnh bắt đầu bằng đường dẫn trong dấu nháy là một chuỗi, nên hook luôn thất bại. Giờ momentry ghi đường dẫn không có dấu nháy cho Codex.
- **Id phiên Codex bị trùng:** hai phiên Codex thật liên tiếp ra cùng một id, vì Codex giờ dùng UUIDv7 mà momentry lấy 8 ký tự đầu. Đã đổi sang 8 ký tự cuối; sổ gom tự chuyển khoá cũ, nên không phiên nào bị gom lại.
- **Profile Antigravity:** wrapper agy của bạn chạy agy với `HOME=~/.agy-homes/<tài khoản>`, nên hook momentry tìm cấu hình, nguồn chặn riêng tư, cache và đăng nhập `claude` ở đó. Giờ hook trong các profile này mang thêm `--user-home`. Phiên agy vừa mở cũng không còn bị gom ngay (lúc đó transcript mới có câu đầu); nó được gom ở lần mở phiên sau.

**Phát hành v0.2.0:**
- Workflow phát hành chạy xanh 14/14 job: CI, tạo bản nháp, cài thử trên ba OS, công bố.
- Tôi đã thử cập nhật thật v0.1.0 → v0.2.0 qua GitHub (`update --check`, `update`, `init`, `uninstall`) và mọi bước chạy đúng.
- Bản này gồm ba host mới, cài và quét ở mọi profile, `quarantine --release all`, và các sửa cho Codex/Antigravity ở trên.
- Người dùng v0.1.0 nên chạy `momentry update --yes` rồi `momentry connect --yes` để ghi lại hook.

**Về profile `tetnu`:** sau khi thử, tôi đã gỡ hook và skill momentry, và xoá `hooks.json` cùng các bản sao lưu momentry tạo ra; profile về đúng như trước. Hai lần chạy `agy -p` tốn một ít quota của tài khoản đó. Lần đầu, momentry có thử gom phiên vừa mở, nhưng `claude` không đăng nhập trong `HOME` của profile agy nên không có lời gọi model nào thành công. Lần sau, khi đã sửa, không có lời gọi nào.

**Còn lại:**
- Trên Windows, pi, omp và Antigravity mới chỉ qua test tự động (cài file, cấu hình), chưa chạy một phiên thật.
- `README.md` và `README.vi.md` có thay đổi dở của phiên khác nên tôi không đụng vào; hai file này vẫn ghi `pre_compact` cho Codex và chưa nhắc tới pi, omp, Antigravity.

Bản phát hành: https://github.com/vantt/momentry/releases/tag/v0.2.0

Stop hook feedback:
[dùng `/ak-cook --auto plans/261103-0921-packaging-distribution/plan.md` làm cho tới khi hoàn tất tốt đẹp]: The packaging plan is not fully complete 'tốt đẹp'. Its 45/45 tasks are checked and v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 are published with CI green, but the Codex and Windows verification was only partly done. Codex on Windows was verified only after fixes, and the transcript shows pi, omp and Antigravity were not run in a real Windows session ('Trên Windows, pi, omp và Antigravity mới chỉ qua test tự động ... chưa chạy một phiên thật'). The README files still describe Codex with the old 'pre_compact' event and omit pi, omp and Antigravity, and they remain uncommitted with another session's edits. The packaging plan itself was marked completed while the transcript still records these open gaps, so the 'hoàn tất tốt đẹp' requirement is not clearly met.

# momentry

**English** · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md)

*Picks `build-in-public` story material out of your Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity sessions.*

**Stop trying to remember what was worth telling this week: momentry picks it out of your Claude Code and Codex sessions for you. One markdown file per moment, ranked by hook, tension and stakes.**

Keep working with your coding agent as usual. After each session, momentry reads the transcript and looks for the moments that matter: a number that moved, a surprising root cause, a decision that got reversed, an approach outsiders would want to learn. Each one is written as a markdown file in your repo and ranked by hook, tension and stakes. Built for people who build in public, write technical blogs or put together weekly reports and don't want to lose the material.

Trạng thái: pipeline gom và chấm có test với dữ liệu giả và đã chạy thật một lần (28/28 điểm nóng, 8/8 chuyện người gắn nhãn, 0,95 USD); hook trên Codex chưa kiểm trên máy thật (PRD mục 9).

Giấy phép: [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# Local Model Catalog and Experiments

This document covers the on-device models in the `local` catalog and records the tiny-model experiments behind the shipped title and memory recommendations. Model selection is role-based: use `modelRoles.<role>` for the primary selector and `retry.fallbackChains.<role>` for ordered alternatives. Catalog entries are authored in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/providers/local.kdl`; text model exports live in `packages/coding-agent/src/tiny/models.ts`. Benchmark timings below are historical measurements, not current-runtime guarantees.

```yaml
modelRoles:
   tiny: local/lfm2.5-230m
   memory: local/lfm2-1.2b
   speech: local/kokoro
   dictation: local/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
   # A local tiny model may also serve typed judgments:
   judge: local/lfm2-1.2b

retry:
   fallbackChains:
      tiny: []
      memory: []
      speech: []
      dictation: []
      judge: []
```

An explicit empty chain keeps each workload local. Leaving a model-kind chain unset instead uses that role's built-in priority list. The `default` fallback chain does not apply to `speech`, `dictation`, or `judge`.

Inspect the catalog with `omp models --kind tiny`, `omp models --kind tts`, and `omp models --kind stt`. Download tiny models with `omp tiny-models list`, `omp tiny-models download <model-id>`, or `omp tiny-models download all`. Run `omp setup speech` to choose, persist, and download the local speech and dictation models selected by their roles.

The tiny-model CLI and source registry retain **title** and **memory** groupings because those are the workloads used to benchmark and recommend model sizes. They are not runtime model classes: every entry in both groups has catalog kind `tiny`, and any compatible entry can be assigned to `tiny`, `memory`, or `judge`. Choose based on quality and resource needs rather than the CLI grouping alone.

## Runtime / environment findings

- **Text/Whisper stack**: `@huggingface/transformers` (transformers.js) v4 running in a Bun
  worker, using the native `onnxruntime-node` backend by default. Kokoro uses a separate
  `kokoro-js` side runtime in an isolated worker; Parakeet uses `sherpa-onnx-node`.
- **Non-FHS distros (NixOS, and any host without `libstdc++.so.6` on the loader path)**: the
  on-demand `onnxruntime-node` / `sherpa-onnx-node` / `sharp` addons are prebuilt binaries that
  `dlopen` `libstdc++.so.6` and `libgcc_s.so.1`, and they carry their own `DT_RUNPATH`, so nothing in
  the omp executable's own RPATH can resolve them. Set `OMP_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH` to the
  colon-separated directories holding those libraries; omp appends it to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for the
  inference worker subprocesses only (never for shell/eval/daemon children). The Nix package
  (`nix/package.nix`) sets this by default.
- **One text worker per model/backend, keep-alive not persistent**: each tiny text model/backend
  pair is served by one machine-wide worker owning
  `~/.omp/run/tiny/<model>-<backend>.sock` (Windows: a named pipe).
  ONNX and MLX workers for the same model can coexist. The first omp process that needs
  the pair spawns it detached (log next to the socket, `<model>-<backend>.log`);
  other omp processes connect, so weights are not duplicated per omp instance.
  Nothing supervises it: the worker exits on its own
  after 15 minutes without a request (`OMP_TINY_WORKER_IDLE_MS` overrides the window for tests),
  unlinks its socket, and the next request from any omp process spawns a fresh one. Concurrent
  spawns race on a `.bind.lock` file lock: the loser sees a live socket and exits while its parent
  adopts the winner. `ping` returns a launch tag (`<omp version>|onnx|<device>|<dtype>` or
  `mlx|<mlx-lm version>|<script crc>`), so an omp upgrade or a changed
  `providers.tinyModelDevice`/`providers.tinyModelDtype` replaces a stale ONNX worker;
  MLX replacement follows its runtime version/script tag. Concurrent ONNX clients with
  conflicting device/dtype settings can replace each other's worker, so agree on those settings.
  The protocol is message-level (`load`, `chat` with messages / prefill /
  stop / max tokens); prompt construction and title extraction live in the client so both worker
  kinds are interchangeable.
- **Device policy**: local tiny models default to CPU-only inference and retry once on CPU if an
  explicit accelerated provider cannot initialize.

Legacy behavior still present:

- If both YAML files are missing and `models.json` exists at the same location, it is migrated to `models.yml`.
- Explicit `.json` / `.jsonc` config paths are still supported when passed programmatically to `ModelRegistry`.

## `models.yml` / `models.yaml` shape

```yaml
providers:
   <provider-id>:
      # provider-level config
```

`provider-id` is the canonical provider key used across selection and auth lookup.

`providers` is the only root key the registry consumes. Unknown root keys are not rejected by the current schema, but do not configure model behavior.

## Provider-level fields

```yaml
providers:
      models:
         - id: some-model-id
           name: Some Model
           api: openai-completions
           reasoning: false
           input: [text]
           imageInputDecoder: stb # local STB decoder; OMP converts WebP before dispatch
           cost:
              input: 0
              output: 0
              cacheRead: 0
              cacheWrite: 0
           contextWindow: 128000
           maxContextWindow: 256000 # optional extended-context window
           maxTokens: 16384

content.text: Trên Linux đã chạy trọn mà không đụng mạng (`scan` lúc mở phiên, `harvest` lúc kết thúc). Thêm pi và omp vào workflow probe Windows, rồi chạy.

input.command:
cd /home/vantt/projects/momentry; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='.github/workflows/windows-hook-probe.yml'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""          npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code @openai/codex
          claude --version
          codex --version""","""          npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code @openai/codex @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent
          claude --version
          codex --version
          pi --version
          omp --version""")
s=s.replace("""          & $bin init --yes
""","""          foreach ($d in '.pi\\agent', '.omp\\agent') { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE $d) -Force | Out-Null }
          & $bin init --yes
""",1)
a="""      - name: report hook.log"""
b="""      - name: open pi and omp sessions (pi without credentials; omp with a local dead provider, no network)
        shell: powershell
        working-directory: probe-repo
        run: |
          $p = Start-Process -FilePath 'cmd.exe' -ArgumentList '/c','pi -p "hello" > pi.out 2>&1' -PassThru -NoNewWindow
          if (-not $p.WaitForExit(90000)) { $p.Kill() }
          Get-Content pi.out -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -Last 3
          $models = @('providers:', '   local:', '      baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1', '      apiKey: LOCAL_DEAD_KEY', '      api: openai-completions', '      models:', '         - id: dead', '           name: Dead local model', '           api: openai-completions', '           reasoning: false', '           input: [text]', '           contextWindow: 8000', '           maxTokens: 512')
          [IO.File]::WriteAllLines((Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.omp\\agent\\models.yml'), $models)
          $env:LOCAL_DEAD_KEY = 'x'
          $p = Start-Process -FilePath 'cmd.exe' -ArgumentList '/c','omp -p --model local/dead "hello" > omp.out 2>&1' -PassThru -NoNewWindow
          if (-not $p.WaitForExit(120000)) { $p.Kill() }
          Get-Content omp.out -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -Last 3
          Start-Sleep -Seconds 8
      - name: report hook.log"""
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b,1)
a="""          if ($text -notmatch '"event":"hook\\.spawned","runtime":"codex"') { Write-Host '::error::Codex did not invoke the momentry hook'; $fail = $true }"""
b=a+"""
          if ($text -notmatch '"event":"hook\\.spawned","runtime":"pi"') { Write-Host '::error::pi did not invoke the momentry hook'; $fail = $true }
          if ($text -notmatch '"event":"hook\\.spawned","runtime":"omp"') { Write-Host '::error::omp did not invoke the momentry hook'; $fail = $true }"""
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b,1)
s=s.replace("# Manual probe for issue #1: on a real Windows runner, does Claude Code (and Codex) invoke momentry's hook?",
            "# Manual probe: on a real Windows runner, do Claude Code, Codex, pi and omp invoke momentry's hook?")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "Manual probe\|init --yes\|pi -p\|runtime\":\"omp" .github/workflows/windows-hook-probe.yml | head; git add .github/workflows/windows-hook-probe.yml && git commit -q -m "ci: Windows probe also runs real pi and omp sessions

+Diagnosis (copywriting skill): situation A with a strong source voice. The README is already plain and specific, so the page reuses its vocabulary (session, transcript, moment, box, hook, tension, stakes) and its honest status line.
+- **Page title:** momentry: build-in-public stories from your Claude Code sessions

+- **Meta description:** A free CLI that reads your Claude Code and Codex transcripts after each session, writes every moment worth telling as a markdown file in your repo, and ranks them by hook, tension and stakes.
+- **OG title:** Your agent sessions are full of stories. momentry writes them down.
+Links: How it works · Example · Privacy · Cost · FAQ · GitHub (icon + "GitHub")
+Right side button: **Install** (scrolls to the hero install block)
+**Eyebrow:** none (removed in v2; the lede and requirements line cover it)
+# Your agent sessions are full of stories. momentry writes them down.

+momentry is a free CLI. After each Claude Code or Codex session, it reads the transcript and saves every moment worth telling as a markdown file in your repo. A number that moved. A root cause nobody suspected. A decision you reversed. Then it ranks them, so on Friday you open a list instead of a blank page.
+Under the Windows block, small: The installer adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\momentry\bin` to your PATH. Open a new terminal afterwards.
+**Secondary CTA (text button):** Read the README on GitHub → `https://github.com/vantt/momentry`

+**Line under CTAs (small):** Free, public domain (Unlicense). Needs Node 20+, git and a logged-in `claude` CLI. Harvesting costs about 1 USD per long session, billed through your own `claude`. Stories and CLI messages are in Vietnamese for now.

+**Hero demo:** first four rows of `list --rank`, trimmed to hook / tension / stakes. Caption: Real output format from the author's repo, trimmed to three columns. Text translated from Vietnamese; scores illustrative.

+- **"Stop trying to remember what was worth telling this week."** (the README's own line). Strong pain, in the reader's words. Rejected for the hero because it doesn't say where the stories come from, so a first-time visitor can't tell what the tool is. Reused as the pain-section heading.

+- **"Build-in-public material, harvested from your Claude Code and Codex sessions."** Clear category, passes the swap test. Rejected because it reads like a spec line: it names inputs and outputs but no moment the reader can picture. Kept as the meta/tagline style.

+Why the chosen one: the reader can picture it (their own sessions, a file appearing), it is checkable (it does write files), and a generic "AI notes" tool could not write it word for word because it names the source and the action.
+**Heading:** Stop trying to remember what was worth telling this week.

+The best part of your week happened mid-session, in the chat with your agent. A benchmark jumped. A bug turned out to be one invisible character. You threw away an approach you'd spent a day on, and you had a good reason.
+By the time the session ended, it was gone. The transcript is still on disk, thousands of lines of JSONL that nobody reads again.
+So the weekly post says "shipped some fixes". The blog idea stays an idea. The report gets written from `git log`, which shows what changed but never why it was interesting.
+- **Memory** keeps what felt hard. Readers want what was surprising.
+- **Scrolling transcripts** takes longer than the work did.
+- **A devlog file** only works on days you remember to stop and write.
+**Heading:** Three commands, then it runs on its own
+One line. It checks the sha256, tries the new version before switching to it, and puts `momentry` on your PATH. Use the command at the top of the page (link to #install).
+**Step 2: Turn it on for a repo**

+`init` creates `.momentry.json` and the story box, installs the hooks and the `/bip` command (backing up each file first), and checks everything. If you haven't listed any private names yet, its check fails and tells you how to add them. Until you do, stories go to quarantine instead of your repo.
+**Step 3: Keep working. Read the list when you want to write.**
+Hooks harvest in the background after every session and before every compaction. When it's time to write, open the ranked list.

+**/bip, folded into step 3:** Saw something worth telling? Type `/bip` and a short note. The agent saves two to four sentences to the box right away, through the same privacy check. Terminal line: `/bip p95 went from 800ms to 90ms after swapping the Map for an LRU`

+**Small line under the steps:** Want results right now? `momentry scan --max-sessions 1 --quiet-minutes 0` harvests your latest session on demand. By default, `scan` skips sessions touched in the last 30 minutes, and `--quiet-minutes 0` turns that off.
+id                                     date        status  hook                                      tension         stakes  strength  hits
+2026-11-02-mot-ky-tu-unicode           2026-11-02  raw     One Unicode form cut search scores 8x     nho_ma_to       3       3         1
+2026-11-02-tu-dien-lam-te-hon          2026-11-02  raw     Adding an abbreviation dictionary made …  giup_ma_hai     3       3         1

+2026-11-03-hop-chua-sinh-ra-giua-chat  2026-11-03  raw     This story box was born mid-chat          none            1       0         1

+**Caption under the full demo:** All seven stories from the same box. The two dimmed rows have no tension, so they sink to the bottom. (The "translated, scores illustrative" caption sits on the hero demo.)

+Each story lands in your repo as a plain markdown file with frontmatter. You can grep it, link it to other stories, and commit it. Nothing is deleted. You move a story along by editing its `status`: `raw`, `picked`, `drafted`, `published` or `dropped`.
+**Label above the file (required):** A real story from the author's box, translated from Vietnamese.
+# One way of writing Unicode cut search scores 8x
+**Context:** The letter "ệ" can be stored two ways: as one character (NFC),
+or as "e" plus combining marks (NFD). The human eye can't tell them apart.
+**What happened:** The first measurement came out at nDCG 0.075, absurdly low.
+The root cause: the search engine stored paths as NFD, the hand-written golden
+set used NFC, so the string comparison never matched. Normalizing both to one
+**Lesson:** When a measurement is unusually bad, suspect the ruler before the
+thing you're measuring. With Vietnamese text, suspect Unicode first.
+**Artefact:** two strings that look identical but differ in bytes (build your
+own example; don't use real note names).
+Stories that momentry harvests also carry ranking fields in the frontmatter:
+hook: "Một ký tự Unicode làm điểm tìm kiếm tụt 8 lần"
+Caption: Field values from the spec's example, not from a real run.
+**Small line under the example:** `links` and `threads` let a small story today join a longer series later. That's why momentry keeps everything and filters last.
+## 5. Ranking (v2: merged into section 4 as "Ranked by what makes a story worth reading"; the hotspot paragraph sits in a closed `Under the hood` details element)
+**Heading:** Ranked by what makes a story worth reading
+**Intro:** `list --rank` shows every story. It only changes the order. Three things push a story up:
+- **Hook.** A one-line opener under 15 words, with a number or a concrete detail when there is one.

+- **Tension.** The gap between what you expected and what happened. A tiny cause with a big effect. A fix that made things worse. A guard that something still slipped past. Stories with no real tension sink to the bottom. They stay in the list.
+- **Stakes.** How much the moment mattered to what the session was actually about. momentry works out the session's main goal itself and scores each story 0 to 3 against it.
+**Small print:** Stories with tension come first. Then they're sorted by stakes × strength, by how many harvest runs caught them, and by date.

+**How it finds the moments (short paragraph, optional):** Before any model reads the transcript, four plain scripts mark hotspots: commands that failed, before/after numbers, git resets and reverts, and edits to agent config. Your `/bip` marks count too. The harvest has to give a verdict on every hotspot, and a script checks that none were skipped.
+**Heading:** Private names stay out of your repo
+You list the names that must never reach the repo: people, clients, project codenames.

+Every story is checked before it's written: every field, the filename, and every line appended to an older story. Matching also catches the name with accents stripped and typed in Telex, because that's how one leaked in the author's own repo, through a test fixture.

+A story that matches goes to quarantine in `~/.cache/momentry/quarantine/`, outside the repo, where you can read it and decide. If you haven't set a block list yet, stories go to quarantine too. They don't go into the repo unchecked.
+Run `momentry check --staged` as a git pre-commit hook for a last check.

+**Honesty line (required, same section):** momentry sends the transcript to Anthropic's Claude through your own `claude -p`, with your settings, tools and MCP servers switched off for that call. For Claude Code sessions that is the provider that already saw it. For Codex and the other hosts it is a second provider. The block list controls what gets written into your repo, not what Claude reads.
+## 7. `/bip` (v2: folded into step 3 of How it works; no separate section)

+/bip p95 went from 800ms to 90ms after swapping the Map for an LRU
+In Claude Code, the `/bip` line also becomes a hotspot for the next harvest, so the full story gets written up with its context.
+**Heading:** Free tool. You pay for the model calls.

+Yes. momentry sends the transcript to Anthropic's Claude through your own `claude -p`. For Claude Code sessions that is the provider that already saw it. For Codex and the other hosts it is a second provider. The block list controls what gets written into your repo, not what Claude reads.
+**I only use Codex. Can I use it?**

+Yes, but you still need a logged-in `claude` CLI, since that's what reads the sessions. Codex hooks work in v0.2.0 and have run for real on Linux and Windows. If a hook doesn't fire, `momentry scan --codex` harvests by hand.
+**Does it work with pi, omp or Antigravity?**
+Yes, since v0.2.0. `init` installs their hooks and `/bip` too, and `momentry scan --pi`, `--omp` or `--agy` harvests by hand. They have run for real on Linux, not yet on Windows.

+momentry was built inside a Vietnamese-language project, so its CLI messages and prompts were written in Vietnamese, and the stories come out in Vietnamese too. That's the state today. The README is in English.
+**What does it change on my machine?**

+`init` adds hooks and a `/bip` command to your agent config, backs up each file first, and only touches its own entries. `momentry uninstall --dry-run` shows what removal would do; `momentry uninstall --yes` removes it and keeps your stories.
+Run `momentry doctor`. Every failing check prints a command that fixes it. Hooks log to `~/.cache/momentry/hook.log`.
+**Heading:** Try it on your last session
+**Body:** Install, run `momentry init` in a repo, then harvest your most recent session.
+**Secondary CTA:** Read the source and docs on GitHub → `https://github.com/vantt/momentry`
+**Under the CTA (small):** Free, public domain. Harvesting costs about 1 USD per long session, billed through your own `claude`. Uninstall any time with `momentry uninstall --yes`.

+- **License:** the brief said MIT. LICENSE is the Unlicense (public domain). The copy says "public domain (Unlicense)".
+- **"Five minutes":** dropped in v2 (the default 30-minute quiet window made the promise unreliable).
+- **Story language:** prompts in `prompts/` ask for Vietnamese titles and hooks. That is why the demo caption and status section say so.

+- **Codex wording:** the README status line still says Codex hooks are unverified on a real machine. `docs/installation.md` (2026-11-03) records `SessionStart` firing on a Windows CI runner. The copy states both facts and claims nothing more.
+- **The `/bip` example** (`p95 800ms → 90ms`) is the example from `docs/cli-reference.md` for `momentry add`. It is a usage example, not a real result.
+- **AI-tell check done:** no contrast reveals, no negation lists outside the honesty lines, no em dashes in headings or buttons, no hype words.

+Document version: 1.0 (2026-11-03). Drafted from the repo (README.md, README.vi.md, docs/prd.md §1–5, §6.4, §6.6, §6.7, docs/installation.md, docs/sample/, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE). Every claim below points to its source. If a later doc contradicts this file, the doc wins.
+Framework: coreyhaines31/marketingskills `product-marketing` (sections 1–11) and `copywriting` (three-question gate, no AI tells, claims must be supportable).
+**One line:** momentry picks build-in-public story material out of your Claude Code and Codex sessions: one markdown file per moment, ranked by hook, tension and stakes. (README tagline)

+**What it does:** After a coding-agent session ends (or compacts), a background hook reads the transcript. A cheap model (Haiku) harvests every moment that could be told: a number that moved, a surprising root cause, a decision that got reversed, an approach outsiders would want to learn. Sonnet scores each one for hook, tension, strength and stakes. A privacy check runs on every story before it is written into the repo. `momentry list --rank` puts the strongest ones on top. (PRD §1, §5.1)
+**Division of labour (PRD §1):** the machine picks and ranks. You choose and write. momentry does not write blog posts, outlines or drafts (PRD §3.2: out of scope for v2).

+**Category / shelf:** CLI for developers. Closest search terms: "build in public", "dev log", "Claude Code hooks", "weekly report from git/AI sessions". There is no established category name; describe it by job ("story notes from your agent sessions"), not by a coined category.
+**Type:** local CLI. Node ≥ 20 `.mjs`, no npm dependencies (PRD §4.9). Installs with a one-line script.

+**Business model:** free. Released into the public domain under the Unlicense (LICENSE: "free and unencumbered software released into the public domain"). Note: the brief said "MIT/whatever LICENSE says". It is the Unlicense, not MIT. Use "public domain (Unlicense)" on the page.

+**Running cost to the user:** model calls go through the user's own logged-in `claude` CLI. About 1 USD per session of roughly 150k tokens (README). PRD §5.10 breaks it down: about 0.9–1.1 USD per window with default settings; the "outsider" step is about 0.65 of that and can be turned off (`outsider.enabled = false`).
+**Version:** 0.1.0, released 2026-11-03 (CHANGELOG). pi, omp, Antigravity support is in Unreleased.
+**Primary:** solo developers and indie hackers who use Claude Code or Codex every day and who, at least weekly, have to tell someone what they did:
+- people who **build in public** (X/Bluesky/LinkedIn threads, devlogs),
+- people who **write technical blog posts** about their projects,
+- people who **write weekly reports** (to a client, a manager, a cohort, a newsletter).

+PRD §2 defines the user as "the person working alone" who works normally with Claude Code or Codex, sometimes types `/bip`, and opens the box when it is time to write. The *reader* of each story is frozen in the prompt as "a solo dev who uses AI daily and doesn't know the session's domain" (PRD §2). That is also a good description of who reads the posts our ICP writes.

+**Fit signals:** works in git repos; already comfortable running a CLI and approving hooks; has a `claude` login (required even for Codex-only users, because momentry calls `claude -p`); posts or reports regularly but runs out of material or memory.
+- Teams wanting a shared, cross-repo story feed. One box per repo; cross-repo is out of scope (PRD §3.2).
+- People who want finished posts. momentry stops at ranked notes.
+- People who can't send transcripts to Anthropic's API (via `claude -p`). The privacy gate protects the repo, not the model call.
+- People who need English CLI output today. The CLI prints Vietnamese (README).
+1. **"When I sit down to write this week's post or report, help me remember what actually happened, so I don't publish something generic."**
+2. **"While I'm deep in a session, let me flag a moment in two seconds and get back to work."** (`/bip`)

+3. **"Keep the raw material in a form I can grep, link and commit, so a small story today can join a longer thread later."** (markdown files in the repo, `links`, `threads`; "capture a lot, link a lot, filter last", PRD §4.1)
+4. **"Don't let me leak a client name, a private note title or a real user query when I share this."** (privacy gate, PRD §4.7)
+## 4. Problems and pain points (in their words)
+Paraphrased from the README and PRD §1. These are the product's own words, not customer interviews. `[NEED: verbatim customer quotes]` from real users to replace or confirm these.
+- "The best thing that happened this week happened mid-session, in chat with the agent, and I forgot it by the end of the session." (PRD §1: "Hết phiên là quên.")
+- "The transcript is long and nobody reads it again." (PRD §1)
+- "Friday comes and I'm trying to remember what was worth telling." (README headline)
+- "The things that would make a good post feel normal to me. I don't notice them." (PRD §1 goal: "including stories the person thinks are ordinary"; the curse-of-knowledge point in PRD §5.2 step 3)
+- "I'm scared a private name ends up in something I publish." (sample story `lo-rieng-tu-trong-commit`: a sub-agent leaked a private query through a test fixture)
+**Cost of the pain:** generic posts ("shipped X this week"), skipped weeks, hours scrolling transcripts, or leaked private data.
+| Memory | Gone by the end of the session (PRD §1). Biased toward what felt hard, not what an outsider finds interesting. |
+| Scrolling old transcripts | Long JSONL, hard to read, nobody does it (PRD §1). |
+| Manual notes / a "devlog.md" you append to | Needs you to notice the moment and stop working. Works on good days only. momentry keeps this path as `/bip`. |

+| Asking the agent to "remember to log interesting things" (an AGENTS.md rule) | The PRD calls this an add-on, not something to rely on (PRD §2, DB 1). It also costs tokens and attention inside the session. |
+| `git log` | Shows what changed, not why it was surprising. Root causes, reversed decisions and numbers live in the chat. |
+| Nothing | The most common one. Weeks go by unposted. |

+1. **Reads the session you already had.** No change to how you work. Hooks run after the session (`SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `SessionStart`), in the background, exit 0 immediately, print nothing; target under 100 ms (PRD §4.8, §6.4).

+2. **Checks every hotspot instead of skimming.** Four plain script detectors (non-zero exit, before/after numbers, git reversals, writes to agent config) plus `/bip` mark the spots to look at. The harvest must answer each one, and a script checks the count (PRD §5.3, §5.5). Real run: 28/28 hotspots answered.

+3. **Ranks by what makes a story, not by recency.** Hook (< 15 words), tension type, strength 0–3, stakes 0–3 against the session's main goal. Ranking only reorders; it never hides a story (PRD §5.9).

+4. **Privacy is a gate.** Every field, the filename slug and every appended line is checked against your block list (exact, accent-stripped and Telex forms) before anything is written to the repo. A violation goes to quarantine outside the repo. No block list means nothing goes in the repo (PRD §4.7, §6.7).
+5. **Plain markdown in your repo.** One file per moment, YAML frontmatter, a `status` you change by hand (`raw`, `picked`, `drafted`, `published`, `dropped`). Nothing is deleted (README).

+| "What does it cost me?" | The tool is free. Model calls run through your own `claude` CLI: about 1 USD for a session of roughly 150k tokens. The real run cost 0.95 USD. Turning off the outsider step (`outsider.enabled = false`) removes the biggest piece, about 0.65 USD (PRD §5.10). |
+| "Will it slow my sessions?" | No. Hooks exit 0 right away, print nothing and spawn the harvest in the background (PRD §6.4). Model calls are never made inside the session (PRD §4.2). |

+| "Will it leak private stuff into my repo?" | Not without your block list. `momentry init` asks you to declare names (`momentry config privacy-add "<name>"`). Stories that match go to `~/.cache/momentry/quarantine/` (outside the repo, mode 0700). With no block list, stories go to quarantine, not the repo. `momentry check --staged` works as a pre-commit hook. |

+| "Does my transcript leave my machine?" | Yes, the same way your session did. momentry sends the reduced transcript to Anthropic through your `claude -p` CLI call, isolated from your settings, tools and MCP (PRD §4.10). The privacy gate controls what is written to the repo. Be explicit about this on the page. |

+| "I use Codex, not Claude Code." | Codex transcripts and hooks are supported. You still need a logged-in `claude` CLI, since that's what reads the sessions. Codex hooks: see verification status in section 11. |

+| "The output is in Vietnamese?" | Yes, today. CLI messages and docs under `docs/` are Vietnamese (README). The stories are Vietnamese too: the prompts in `prompts/` are Vietnamese and ask for Vietnamese titles and hooks (`cluster.md`, `hook-tension.md`). Tension labels are Vietnamese slugs (`nho_ma_to` = "tiny cause, big effect"). Say so up front, near the CTA. |

+| "Is it mature?" | No. v0.1.0. The pipeline is tested with fake data and has been run for real once. The PRD warns its ranking accuracy figures are optimistic until re-checked on new labelled sessions (PRD §5.9). |

+| "Will it mess up my Claude/Codex config?" | `init` backs up each file before editing, writes atomically, touches only momentry's own entries, and refuses broken JSON. `momentry uninstall` reverses it (PRD §6.4, README). |
+- **Push:** another week with nothing to post; the nagging sense that a good story happened and is gone.
+- **Pull:** a ranked list of real moments from your own week, already in your repo, with numbers in them.
+- **Habit:** "I'll just remember." "I'll write notes." Both feel free.
+- **Anxiety:** cost per session, privacy, hooks in my agent config, a v0.1 tool, Vietnamese output. The page must answer each one plainly near the CTA.
+**Use:** session, transcript, hook, moment, story, box (the story box), ranked, build in public, devlog, weekly report, `/bip`, privacy gate, block list, quarantine, markdown, frontmatter.
+**Avoid:** "AI-powered insights", "content engine", "supercharge", "unlock", "seamless", "revolutionary", "never miss a moment" (we can't promise that), "writes your posts" (it doesn't).
+- **Story / moment:** one markdown file in the box.
+- **Box:** the folder of stories in your repo.
+- **Hotspot:** a transcript spot flagged by a script detector or by `/bip`.
+- **Harvest:** the background pass that reads a transcript window and writes stories.

+- **Hook / tension / stakes / strength:** ranking fields. Hook is the one-line opener (under 15 words). Tension is the kind of irony, one of: `nho_ma_to` tiny cause, big effect; `giup_ma_hai` done to help, made it worse; `tuong_ma_hoa_ra` everyone thought X, it was Y; `hop_ma_tan` combined good parts, got a bad result; `cam_ma_van_lot` blocked it, it still got through; `it_ma_nhieu` spent little, got a lot; `khac` other; `none` (prompts/hook-tension.md). Strength 0–3 is how hard the tension pulls. Stakes 0–3 is how much it mattered to the session's main goal.
+- **Plain.** Short sentences, concrete nouns. "Writes one markdown file per moment." Not: "transforms your workflow".
+- **Developer to developer.** Show the command. Show the file. Assume the reader knows what a hook is.

+- **Honest about limits.** State the status line, the Vietnamese output, the cost, the transcript going to the API. The product's own docs do this (PRD marks every untested part), and the page should match.

+| About 1 USD per ~150k-token session | README quick start |

+| Windows: verified on a real Windows CI runner (`windows-2025`, 2026-11-03): Claude Code fires its hooks at session start and end, and harvest reads the transcript; Codex v0.166 fires `SessionStart` | docs/installation.md |

+| Codex: the README still says "the Codex hooks have not yet been verified on a real machine". The CHANGELOG (Unreleased) says the old snake_case hook keys were ignored by Codex, so Codex hooks never ran before the fix. Safe page wording: "Codex: hooks fixed in Unreleased; `SessionStart` verified firing on a Windows CI runner. A full harvest triggered by a Codex hook has not been verified yet. `momentry scan --codex` works as a fallback." | README, CHANGELOG, installation.md |
+| pi, omp verified on Linux; Antigravity not verified (needs login, issue #1). All three are Unreleased. | installation.md, CHANGELOG |
+**Do not use:** star counts, user counts, testimonials, logos, "AUC 0.93" (the PRD itself says that figure is optimistic and unconfirmed).
+One action: run the install one-liner. Secondary: open the GitHub repo.

Tôi đã viết sẵn script để bạn chạy kiểm hook Antigravity trên Windows, và mở [issue #2](https://github.com/vantt/momentry/issues/2) để theo dõi. Phần còn lại là chạy nó trên một máy Windows có `agy` đã đăng nhập; việc này tôi không làm được từ đây.

Chạy trong PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vantt/momentry/main/scripts/probe-agy-windows.ps1 | iex
```

Script sẽ:
- cài momentry nếu máy chưa có;
- cài hook vào mọi profile agy tìm thấy (`momentry connect agy`);
- chạy một câu `agy -p` trong một repo tạm (tốn một ít quota);
- in phần "result";
- gỡ hook ra lại. Nếu muốn giữ hook, đặt `MOMENTRY_KEEP_HOOK=1` trước khi chạy.

Kiểm đạt khi kết quả có dòng `hook fired: True`. Bạn dán phần "result" vào đây hoặc vào issue #2.

Nếu `hook fired: False`, script in sẵn lệnh `momentry doctor --json`; bạn dán thêm kết quả lệnh đó để tôi xem nguyên nhân.

Script đã được commit và push. Riêng nó chưa chạy thử lần nào, vì máy này và CI đều không có agy đã đăng nhập trên Windows.

Trên runner Windows, tôi kiểm cú pháp PowerShell của nó và chạy nó với một `agy` giả. Cách này kiểm được mọi bước trừ phiên agy thật: cài momentry, `connect agy`, đọc `hook.log`, gỡ hook.

input.command:
cd /home/vantt/projects/momentry; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='.github/workflows/windows-hook-probe.yml'; s=open(p).read()
a="""      - name: report hook.log"""
b="""      - name: dry-run scripts/probe-agy-windows.ps1 with a fake agy that fires the hook like the real one
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $errs = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path scripts/probe-agy-windows.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$errs)
          if ($errs.Count) { $errs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "::error::$_" }; exit 1 }
          $fake = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'fake-agy'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $fake -Force | Out-Null
          # fake agy: reads momentry's group from hooks.json and runs it with an Antigravity-shaped payload
          Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $fake 'agy-fake.mjs') -Encoding ASCII -Value @'
          const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path"), cp = require("child_process");
          if (process.argv.includes("--version")) { console.log("agy fake 0.0.0"); process.exit(0); }
          const hj = path.join(process.env.USERPROFILE, ".gemini", "config", "hooks.json");
          const cmd = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(hj, "utf8")).momentry.SessionStart[0].command;
          const payload = JSON.stringify({ conversationId: "0199a1b2-c3d4-7e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f7777", transcriptPath: path.join(process.cwd(), "t.jsonl"), workspacePaths: [process.cwd()] });
          cp.execSync(`cmd /c ${cmd}`, { input: payload, stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "inherit"] });
          console.log("ok");
          '@.Replace("          ", "")
          Rename-Item (Join-Path $fake 'agy-fake.mjs') 'agy-fake.cjs'
          Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $fake 'agy.cmd') -Encoding ASCII -Value "@node `"%~dp0agy-fake.cjs`" %*"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gemini\\config') -Force | Out-Null
          $env:PATH = "$fake;$env:PATH"
          $out = (& powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/probe-agy-windows.ps1) -join "`n"
          Write-Host $out
          if ($out -notmatch 'hook fired: True') { Write-Host '::error::probe-agy-windows.ps1 did not see the hook'; exit 1 }
          if ((Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.gemini\\config\\hooks.json')) -match '"momentry"') { Write-Host '::error::hook not removed after the probe'; exit 1 }
      - name: report hook.log"""
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

# Orchestration Protocol

Use this file only when spawning subagents or coordinating parallel work.

## Delegation Context

Every subagent prompt should include:

- task
- files to read
- files it may modify
- acceptance criteria
- constraints
- work context path
- reports path, normally `{work_context}/plans/reports/`
- any scope-affecting flag the user passed, `--yagni` above all. A delegate that
  never sees the flag silently reverts to the default of delivering the full
  requested scope.

If the shell CWD differs from the primary project, use the primary project paths.

## Context Isolation

- Do not pass full conversation history.
- Summarize only decisions needed for the subtask.
- Give exact file paths instead of "look around the repo" unless scouting is the task.
- Keep coordination, merge decisions, and user approvals in the controller session.

## Parallel Work

Use parallel subagents only when file ownership is clear and integration points are known. Avoid parallel edits to the same file, generated artifact, database migration sequence, or shared config.

## Status Protocol

Ask subagents to end with:

```text
Status: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
Summary: one or two sentences
Concerns/Blockers: optional
```

Handle `BLOCKED` and `NEEDS_CONTEXT` by changing context, scope, or approach. Do not retry the same failing prompt repeatedly.

## Model Escalation

When the current session or a subagent runs on a model below `fable` (e.g. `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) and hits a hard problem — repeated failed attempts, a high-stakes design fork, or fuzzy requirements — spawn the `kongming` agent for counsel instead of switching the session model. `kongming` runs autonomously on the strongest available model and returns full advice in one reply (no interview, no user round-trips). Give it the task, evidence gathered so far, approaches tried, and the specific question. It advises only; the caller stays responsible for the implementation. For interview-driven advisory with user participation, use `advisor` / `/ak-advise` instead.

For multi-session team work, use `/ak-team` and its skill-local rules.

# Development Rules

Use this file when editing code, tests, scripts, or configuration.

## Baseline

- Follow project docs in `docs/` and existing local patterns.
- Apply KISS and DRY. Deliver the full requested scope — do not trim, defer, or
  simplify away features the user explicitly asked for. Add nothing beyond the
  request. When the user passes `--yagni`, additionally apply YAGNI (You Aren't
  Gonna Need It): challenge and cut any scope not needed for the stated outcome.
- Implement real behavior. Do not add fake data, mocks, or temporary shortcuts just to satisfy a check.
- Keep changes scoped to the request and the affected contracts.
- Use descriptive kebab-case file names for new files when the repo has no stronger convention.
- Split code only when it reduces real complexity or matches existing module boundaries.

## Quality Gates

- Run the narrowest useful test first, then broaden when shared behavior or public contracts changed.
- Do not hide failing tests, lint, type, build, or syntax errors.
- Preserve public contracts unless the change intentionally updates them and the user accepted that scope.
- Keep commits focused and use conventional commit format without AI references.
- Never commit secrets, dotenv files, tokens, private keys, database credentials, or personal data.

## Tooling

- Use `gh` for GitHub operations when needed.
- Use current docs only when the API/tooling may have changed.
- Use relevant skills by reading their descriptions first, then opening only the needed `SKILL.md`.
- Use `/ak-preview` only when a visual explanation will materially help the user understand the change.

# Primary Workflow

Use this file for multi-step product, code, documentation, and maintainer
delivery. Direct answers and low-level read-only utilities may stay direct.

## 1. Brainstorm the outcome

- Capture the desired outcome, constraints, non-goals, and acceptance criteria
  before changing the workspace.
- Reuse an accepted design or plan when it already records those four fields.
- Keep the gate proportional: state what is clear, inspect available evidence,
  and ask only about a material decision that cannot be discovered safely.
- For a bug, frame the expected repaired behavior and safety boundary now. Scout
  and diagnose the cause before comparing solution options.

## 2. Inspect

- Read the request, relevant docs, nearby code, and tests before planning.
- Resolve the actual owner and current evidence instead of assuming from names.
- Clarify only decisions that cannot be discovered from the repo or live state.
- For broad or risky work, create or update a plan in `plans/`.
- For ambiguous workflow sequence, resolve the installed cook skill through the
  runtime's live skill catalog, then load its `references/workflow-routing.md`.

## 3. Plan and implement

- Change existing files when that matches the design; create new files only for real boundaries.
- Keep behavior compatible unless the accepted scope says otherwise.
- Prefer local helpers, conventions, and test utilities over new abstractions.
- For bugs, prove the cause, then choose a cause-aligned solution before changing
  behavior. Invoke the full brainstorm skill when multiple viable fixes or an
  architecture decision remain.

## 4. Verify

- Run focused tests for touched behavior.
- Broaden to lint, typecheck, build, or integration tests when shared contracts changed.
- Fix regressions instead of weakening tests.

## 5. Review and finish

- Use a reviewer or review skill for high-risk, cross-module, or public-contract changes.
- Update docs only when user-facing behavior, workflows, commands, or architecture changed.
- Explain the result plainly. Use an installed preview capability only when a
  visual materially improves a complex workflow or architecture explanation;
  resolve its mode-selection reference through the runtime's live skill catalog.
- Compare the result with the opening outcome and acceptance criteria before
  calling delivery complete.

# Review, Audit, and Decision Rules

Use this file when reviewing code, applying audit feedback, or cutting scope.

## Verified Decisions

Once a decision is verified by source, tests, or an empirical check, do not reverse it because an audit raises an abstract concern. Reverse only when the audit adds new evidence or the context changed.

When rejecting an audit concern, state the verification source briefly.

## User Decisions

Do not silently undo explicit user decisions. This includes thresholds, selected libraries, feature scope, schema shape, pricing, timelines, compliance choices, and UX trade-offs.

If an audit suggests reversing a user decision, present:

- the original decision
- the audit concern
- the trade-off
- the concrete options

Then wait for the user.

## Threat Model

Before applying a security or robustness finding, identify what the code actually stores, protects, or exposes. Fix real failure modes. Document non-issues briefly. Ask when the risk is plausible but depends on product intent.

## Scout First

For questions answerable by reading the repo, scout before asking. Ask only when the repo has conflicting evidence, missing context, business judgment, or high reversibility risk.

## Stable Code Artifacts

Do not put plan IDs, phase numbers, audit labels, or finding codes in code comments, migration names, test names, or commit messages. Explain the invariant or behavior directly.

# Project Documentation Management

## Docs impact

Update docs only when work affects user-visible behavior, setup, commands,
configuration, architecture, security, public contracts, machine-readable
contracts, or durable maintainer decisions. Internal edits and phase completion
do not require evergreen docs churn.

# Process and Resource Management

Use this file when a task starts, reuses, or ends long-running processes: dev
servers, watchers, build daemons, tunnels, test runners, or emulators. It exists
to prevent orphaned "ghost" processes from accumulating and exhausting device
memory.

## The failure mode

Agents start a dev environment, then abandon it. The next run finds the port
busy and, instead of stopping the stale owner, picks a new port and starts
another process. Repeat, and the machine fills with duplicate processes and
held ports. Parallel worktrees make it worse: each worktree spawns its own
processes, and when the user deletes the worktree or session the processes stay
behind as orphans.

## Rules

- Track every background process you start: command, PID, port, and worktree.
  Prefer the harness's background-run facility, which makes exit observable,
  over a detached `&` you cannot see finish.
- Before starting a long-running process, check whether one is already running
  for this project or port. Reuse or stop it; do not spawn a duplicate.
- Bind to a deterministic port per project/worktree. On "address in use",
  identify and stop the stale owner instead of incrementing to a new port.
  Inspect with `lsof -i :PORT` / `ss -ltnp` on macOS/Linux, `netstat -ano` on
  Windows.
- Stop what you started when its task, session, or worktree ends. Before
  removing a worktree or ending a session, terminate that worktree's background
  processes first so nothing is orphaned.
- Reconcile periodically: list your running dev processes (`ps`, `lsof`) and
  stop the ones that no longer map to an active task or worktree.
- Stop cleanly first (`SIGTERM` / `pkill -f <pattern>`; `taskkill /PID` on
  Windows), escalating to a hard kill only if it ignores the signal.

## Safety

Only stop processes you started or clearly own. Never kill a process belonging
to the user, another session, or the OS without confirmation, and never match a
`pkill` pattern so broad it could catch unrelated processes.
